minor.issue: The event is inserted (marked consumed) BEFORE the re-fetch. If the re-fetch fails, Bolna's retry of the same payload counts as a duplicate and never re-fetches, so the call stays needs_refetch=true forever unless a reconciler or poller exists. Phase 4B needs a needs_refetch reconciler, or the event should only be marked processed after a successful apply.
_record_event treats ANY insert exception as a duplicate (bare except), so Mongo errors are silently reported as {duplicate: true}. Catch DuplicateKeyError only.

Out-of-order guard uses '<', so equal-rank terminal statuses (e.g. completed -> failed, both rank 5) overwrite each other, including response and completed_at. Since only re-fetched data is applied this is low risk. Consider freezing once terminal and re-applying only the same status.

source_ip takes the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client can spoof. ip_allowlisted is informational only (not enforced), so there is no security impact now. Do not enforce the allowlist on this value in 4B without using the trusted ingress hop.
A rejected 'execution mismatch' leaves no flag or audit on the ai_calls doc, and the event is consumed, so it is silently dropped. Consider setting a mismatch flag for ops visibility.

issues: The Agent ID input is pre-filled with the full agent id in plain text, while the helper says 'Current: ••••••••7a9ba5' (inconsistent masking). Not a secret, but it is inconsistent.

action_items: Before Phase 4B: add a needs_refetch reconciler/poller, or record the webhook event as processed only after a successful re-fetch and apply, so failed re-fetches can be retried.
Narrow the except in _record_event to pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError.
Optional: freeze terminal status in apply_execution and flag execution-mismatch rejections on the call doc.

Matched path writes to ai_calls only: needs_refetch on re-fetch failure, or apply_execution with re-fetched data after the id and agent_id match. The webhook body is never applied.

Token check uses hmac.compare_digest on a sha256 hash and returns 404 when no token is configured. The isinstance(dict) guard (line 107) fixes the earlier 500 on non-dict JSON. The 500 seen in old logs comes from before that guard.
